diagnostic_evidence.quote: Entropy admissibility is incorporated in integral form to ensure uniqueness and physical consistency of the weak solution.
ensures uniqueness in many important cases, including scalar conservation laws and several physically relevant systems
E_R(U_\theta) = \sup_{k \in \mathbb{R}, \varphi \in \mathcal{A}} \mathcal{R}_{k,\varphi}(U_\theta)
We emphasize that this convergence result is currently valid only for scalar conservation laws.

issues.failure_explanation: The paper states unconditionally, for general systems, that weak conservation plus the inequality for one fixed entropy pair (the only one used in the loss) characterizes the entropy solution and ensures uniqueness. The source itself hedges this ('in many important cases'). Its own analysis needs the whole Kruzkov family over all k in R, and it is restricted to scalar laws. Nothing in the paper shows that one entropy pair selects a unique solution for the Euler or shallow-water systems treated.

failure_location.quote: Together, \eqref{eq:weak_conservation} and~\eqref{eq:entropy_inequality} characterize the entropy solution of~\eqref{eq:conservation_law}

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Qualify the claims: uniqueness only where it is known (e.g. the full Kruzkov family for scalar laws). For systems, present the single-entropy penalty as an admissibility heuristic.
issues.overall_effect: The advertised selection of the unique physically admissible solution by L_ent is unsupported, particularly for the system experiments.
issues.title: A single entropy pair is claimed to characterize and select the unique entropy solution
issues.why_classification: Rewording suffices, but it withdraws a substantive advertised property (uniqueness/selection) for the system cases.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Since $\varphi \in \mathcal{A}$, its Lipschitz constant is bounded by $1$. The factor containing $\varphi$ is therefore neutralized:
\frac{\big(\max\{0,\,E_\theta(D_k)\}\big)^2}{|D_k|}
For any partition $\{D_i\}_{i=1}^{N_D}$ of $\Omega \times (0,T)$
Sample space--time subdomains $\{D_k\}_{k=1}^{N_D}$ at multiple scales.

issues.failure_explanation: Integrating by parts gives a phi-weighted volume integral of the divergence. On each D_i this cannot be bounded by Lip(phi) times the unweighted box residual, because the integrand can change sign inside D_i. Counterexample with the trivial partition D_1 = Omega_T: let U_theta = U_0 be a smooth, time-independent, nonconstant profile with U_0(-1) = U_0(1). Both box residuals vanish, so L_cons = L_ent = 0. Yet U_0 is not a weak solution: for k < min U_0, R_{k,phi} = -int phi d_x F(U_0), which is nonzero for suitable phi. There are further gaps. R_ent(D_i,k) is never defined, and it depends on k, whereas L_ent uses one fixed pair (eta,q). The proof bounds |R_ent| although L_ent penalizes only positive parts. The training loss uses sampled overlapping volumes, not a partition. With the stated sign, an admissible shock solution even has E_R > 0.

failure_location.quote: Applying the divergence theorem on each $D_i$, the continuous residual translates into boundary flux integrals, corresponding exactly to the local conservation residual $R_{\mathrm{cons}}(D_i)$ and entropy residual $R_{\mathrm{ent}}(D_i, k)$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: No complete source-supported repair identified; at minimum, a repair must control the Kruzkov defect for all k and all Lipschitz phi from quantities the loss actually controls. This would require, for example, losses over all Kruzkov entropies and a family of boxes fine enough to resolve the test functions, with explicit dependence on box size and on the residual's variation.
issues.overall_effect: The link between the training losses and the weak entropy defect is false. Theorem 2 and the claimed rigorous L^1 rate lose their foundation.
issues.title: Lemma 1: invalid reduction of the Kruzkov weak residual to control-volume losses
issues.why_classification: The central analytic lemma is false as stated, and no comparable version follows without a new proof architecture. The main convergence theorem collapses with it.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: The weak conservation loss is defined as the volume-weighted average of the squared Euclidean norm of these residuals:

issues.failure_explanation: L_cons includes the prefactor 1/N_D, so sum_i |R_i|^2/|D_i| = N_D L_cons. Cauchy-Schwarz therefore yields sqrt(N_D |Omega_T| L_cons), not sqrt(|Omega_T| L_cons); the same holds for L_ent. The stated bound is off by sqrt(N_D), which grows as more control volumes are used.

failure_location.quote: Recognizing that $\sum |D_i| = |\Omega \times (0,T)|$ and substituting the definitions of $L_{\mathrm{cons}}(\theta)$ and $L_{\mathrm{ent}}(\theta)$ defined in Section 3

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Insert sqrt(N_D) in the lemma, or use un-normalized losses, and propagate the factor into K_opt.
issues.overall_effect: The constant in Lemma 1, and hence K_opt in Theorem 2, is understated by a power of N_D. The bound degrades under refinement.
issues.title: Lemma 1 drops a factor sqrt(N_D) from the 1/N_D-averaged losses
issues.why_classification: This is a local constant correction. The functional form and theta-independence for fixed N_D survive.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: \varphi \in C_c^\infty(\Omega \times (0,T)) : \varphi \ge 0
All experiments are performed on the domain $\Omega = [-1,1]$ with final time $T=1$.
the flux integration across this face directly enforces the prescribed boundary conditions

issues.failure_explanation: Omega is a bounded domain, no boundary conditions are imposed, and the test functions in A are compactly supported in the interior, so E_R does not see boundary data. Counterexample: take F(u)=u on [-1,1], u_0 = 0 and u = 0. Let v(x,t) = g(t-(x+1)) with g smooth and g = 0 on (-inf,0]. Then v is a classical solution, so E_R(v) = 0, v(.,0) = u_0 and TV is bounded. The right-hand side of the estimate is 0, yet v(.,T) differs from 0. Hence 'unique entropy solution' is also meaningless without boundary data.

failure_location.quote: Let $u$ be the unique entropy solution of \eqref{eq:conservation_law}

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restrict Theorems 1-2 to the Cauchy problem on R^d, or to domains and times not influenced by the boundary (via finite propagation speed). Alternatively, add boundary entropy terms to the defect with a corresponding estimate.
issues.overall_effect: The cited estimate, and Theorem 2 built on it, do not hold in the bounded-domain setting where WE-PINNs are formulated and tested.
issues.title: Stated Bouchut-Perthame estimate is false on bounded domains without boundary conditions
issues.why_classification: A comparable whole-space or localized result survives, but with a limited loss of scope relative to the bounded-domain setting.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: C \sqrt{TV(u_0) \cdot \sup_{t \in [0,T]} TV(v(\cdot, t)) \cdot \sqrt{E_R(v)}}
\leq K_{\mathrm{opt}} \cdot \left(L_{\mathrm{cons}}(\theta)^{1/4} + L_{\mathrm{ent}}(\theta)^{1/4}\right)

issues.failure_explanation: Theorem 1 gives error <= C sqrt(TV(u_0) M) E_R^{1/4}. The second line of Step 4 instead raises the bound on E_R to the power 1/2. For small E_R we have E_R^{1/4} > E_R^{1/2}, so that inequality is false. Correctly combining Lemma 1 with Theorem 1 yields |Omega_T|^{1/8}(L_cons^{1/8} + L_ent^{1/8}), not the claimed 1/4 rate.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restate the theorem with exponent 1/8 and K_opt = C sqrt(TV(u_0) M)|Omega_T|^{1/8}.
issues.overall_effect: The advertised explicit L^1 rate, and the remark built on it, are overstated. Even granting the inputs, only an L^{1/8} rate follows.
issues.title: Theorem 2 exponent error: the chain gives L^{1/8}, not L^{1/4}
issues.why_classification: The correction necessarily halves the exponent of the headline convergence rate, a material worsening of an advertised rate guarantee.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Then, there exists a constant $K_{\mathrm{opt}}$ independent of $\theta$ such that
defining $K_{\mathrm{opt}} = C \sqrt{TV(u_0) M} \cdot |\Omega \times (0,T)|^{1/4}$
L_{\mathrm{TVD}}(\theta) \approx \max_{j=1,\dots,N_t} \sum_{k=1}^{N_x-1} |U_\theta(x_{k+1}, t_j) - U_\theta(x_k, t_j)|
To guarantee this condition, we introduce a TVD regularization term:

issues.failure_explanation: A penalty term in a weighted sum does not guarantee any bound. The implemented estimator, a sum of differences at finitely many sampled points and times, is always a lower bound for sup_t TV, so minimizing it certifies nothing about the true TV. K_opt contains M. If M depends on theta, as 'for some constant M' allows, then K_opt is not independent of theta, and convergence as the losses tend to 0 fails along sequences with M_theta growing without bound.

failure_location.quote: The TVD regularization guarantees $\sup_{t \in [0,T]} TV(U_\theta(\cdot, t)) \leq M$ for some constant $M$;

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Assume explicitly a uniform bound sup_theta sup_t TV(U_theta) <= M over the considered family, let K_opt depend on M, and drop the claim that the penalty guarantees it.
issues.overall_effect: The theta-independence of K_opt and the convergence conclusion rest on an unestablished uniform TV bound. The claim that TVD regularization guarantees the Bouchut-Perthame hypothesis is unsupported.
issues.title: Uniform TV bound assumed to follow from the TVD penalty; K_opt depends on theta through M
issues.why_classification: This is a limited weakening: the result becomes conditional on an extra uniform hypothesis, but its form survives.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: For regular, structured grids, the rate can be improved to $1/2$ \cite{bouchut1998}.
\leq K_{\mathrm{opt}} \cdot \left(L_{\mathrm{cons}}(\theta)^{1/4} + L_{\mathrm{ent}}(\theta)^{1/4}\right)

issues.failure_explanation: The exponent results from chaining upper bounds (Cauchy-Schwarz in Lemma 1 and the square roots in Theorem 1). No lower bound or example is given, so optimality is not established. The exponent 1/2 on structured grids is likewise unsupported, since no grid structure enters Theorem 1.

failure_location.quote: The convergence rate of $1/4$ is optimal for arbitrary control volume partitions.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Delete or qualify the optimality and grid-improvement claims.
issues.overall_effect: Readers are misled about the sharpness of the analysis.
issues.title: Unsupported optimality claim for the 1/4 rate and improvement on grids
issues.why_classification: Removing an unproven remark affects no theorem or guarantee.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: This construction guarantees $U_\theta(x,0) \equiv U_0(x)$, eliminating the initial condition error term from the convergence analysis.
Construct temporal ansatz: $U_\theta(x,t) = (1-\tau(t))U_0(x) + \tau(t)\mathcal{N}_\theta(x,t)$

issues.failure_explanation: With tau(0)=0, the method's output at t=0 equals U_0 exactly, so all t=0 errors should vanish. The tables instead report nonzero t=0 errors for WE-PINNs, including a relative L^inf error of 0.795 for the Burgers shock and nonzero errors for shallow water. So the reported networks did not use the described construction, or the reported errors are inconsistent.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Clarify the implementation actually used. Either re-run the experiments with the ansatz, or report results consistent with exact initial data.
issues.overall_effect: The numerical results cannot be attributed to the method as specified. Step 1 of Theorem 2 (zero initial error) does not apply to the reported networks.
issues.title: Reported nonzero t=0 errors contradict the exact initial-condition ansatz
issues.why_classification: The experimental validation must be re-established, but the method and theory are not themselves changed.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: In all cases, the entropy functions are convex and the corresponding entropy fluxes satisfy the compatibility condition with the physical flux

abla_U q^{(j)}(U) = 
abla_U \eta(U)\,
abla_U F^{(j)}(U)

issues.failure_explanation: For 1D SWE with eta = h u^2/2 + g h^2/2, we have grad eta = (gh - u^2/2, u). Then grad eta * F'(U) = (ghu - u^3, 3u^2/2 + gh), which is the gradient of q = h u^3/2 + g h^2 u. The stated q = eta u lacks the term g h^2 u/2 and violates compatibility. Even smooth exact solutions then give d_t eta + d_x(eta u) = -d_x(g h^2 u/2), which is not identically zero. The SWE entropy loss therefore penalizes exact entropy solutions.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Use q = (h|u|^2/2 + g h^2)u, i.e. q = (eta + g h^2/2)u. Re-run the SWE experiments if the stated flux was used.
issues.overall_effect: The entropy residual and entropy loss for the 1D and 2D shallow-water experiments, as specified, are inconsistent. The admissibility enforcement claimed for SWE is unreliable.
issues.title: Shallow-water entropy flux is wrong (missing pressure-work term)
issues.why_classification: The formula fix is local, but the SWE results obtained with the incorrect entropy loss may need recomputation.
